tool.name: lighthouse
tool.invocation: npx lighthouse@12.6.1 (lhci 0.15.1-bundled major); node 22.14 blocks lighthouse@13 which requires >=22.19

measurement_target.note: Local preview of the production static artifact (BASE_PATH omitted, served at root). Staging URL https://wolfwdavid.github.io/michelle_ngo_three/ returned HTTP 404 at measurement time (deploy not live on this branch), so the local production-build preview is the conservative stand-in. The production apex (BASE_PATH="") will measure marginally faster than the subpath staging build; this local-root measurement is representative of the apex artifact.
measurement_target.lcp_element: hero poster static/posters/vimeo-264677021.jpg (loading=eager, fetchpriority=high); hero iframe deferred via createHeroDefer per Phase 5 — Pitfall 3: NOT a static-WebP , so _four AVIF escalation does not map

config.throttlingProfile: lighthouse mobile default (Slow-4G — simulated 4G per D-17)
config.preset: NONE (desktop preset deliberately avoided — would disable Slow-4G and hide a mobile LCP miss)

before.label: Initial Task 3 measurement (poster preload still in HeroAmbient.svelte child <svelte:head>)

escalation.trigger: Task 4 human-verify checkpoint — user decision: "Preload poster + re-measure" (D-17 poster-first menu option a; NOT _four's AVIF <picture> route — Pitfall 3).
escalation.change: Moved the hero-poster preload <link rel=preload as=image fetchpriority=high> OUT of HeroAmbient.svelte's child <svelte:head> and into each consuming route's PAGE-level head (src/routes/+page.svelte for `/`, src/routes/about/+page.svelte for `/about`). The href is derived from the same data helpers HeroAmbient uses (base + getPosterFor(getById(producerReelId))) so there is zero path/literal drift. Exactly one preload per route (de-duplicated).
escalation.honest_finding: Page-level vs child-component head placement does NOT reorder the preload ahead of SvelteKit's JS modulepreloads: SvelteKit emits all `%sveltekit.head%` JS modulepreload <link>s at the top of <head>, and ALL user <svelte:head> content (page OR child) follows. Reordering ahead of the JS manifest would require editing app.html to inject before %sveltekit.head% (out of scope, risky). The effective lever remains fetchpriority="high", which the browser's resource scheduler honors independent of DOM order. The measured gain is therefore modest but real, and run-to-run variance tightened markedly (all 3 after-runs within 11ms; perf score 0.94–0.95 on every run vs 0.89–0.94 before).

after.label: Post-escalation re-measurement (poster preload at page-level head, fetchpriority=high)

verdict.outcome: ACCEPTED for this run. Per the Task 4 checkpoint directive: the LCP gate is WARNING-ONLY in this plan and Plan 07-04 flips warn->error pre-cutover. The 306ms residual miss against the 2.5s simulated-Slow-4G budget remains a WARNING; do NOT loop on further escalations. Residual-reduction levers available for 07-04 if the blocking flip requires them: (a) AVIF poster variant [PERF-V2-02, deferred], (b) tune createHeroDefer timing, (c) re-measure on the faster production apex (BASE_PATH='' — no subpath; this local-root measurement is the conservative stand-in), or (d) the _four branch (defer to post-launch real-user telemetry).
verdict.summary: After moving the poster preload to the page-level head + keeping fetchpriority=high, median / LCP improved 2859ms -> 2806ms (-53ms) with markedly tighter variance and perf 0.91 -> 0.95. LCP still MISSES the 2500ms budget by 306ms — ACCEPTABLE under the warning-only posture; the 07-04 pre-cutover flip owns the blocking decision.

vu7_remediation.label: 260610-vu7 remediation (app.html preload hoist ahead of JS manifest + 2.5s iframe defer)

tool.name: lighthouse
tool.invocation: npx lighthouse@12.6.1 http://localhost:4183/ --only-categories=performance --output=json --chrome-flags="--headless=new --no-sandbox" (default mobile preset, simulated Slow-4G)

measurement_target.note: Local preview of the production static artifact (BASE_PATH omitted, root). Same conservative stand-in methodology as the 07-03 measurement; staging URL 404s on this branch.
measurement_target.lcp_element: hero poster (confirmed via largest-contentful-paint-element audit)

vu7_remediation.change: (1) Hoisted the hero-poster <link rel=preload as=image fetchpriority=high> into src/app.html BEFORE the SvelteKit head token so it precedes ALL JS modulepreloads in DOM order (build/index.html structurally verified by scripts/check-preload-order.mjs). (2) Removed the now-redundant page-level preloads from src/routes/+page.svelte and src/routes/about/+page.svelte. (3) Eased createHeroDefer idle/timeout window 1000ms -> 2500ms to keep the hero iframe fetch out of the LCP paint window (interaction trigger unchanged).

network_diagnostic.poster_request: vimeo-264677021.jpg fetched FIRST at networkRequestTime=13ms, networkEndTime=18ms, priority=High — the preload hoist works perfectly at the network layer (poster is on the wire and complete in the first ~18ms, ahead of all JS modulepreloads).
network_diagnostic.interpretation: LCP is NOT image-download bound. The poster is available at ~18ms but cannot PAINT until first paint, and FCP sits at ~2715ms on this measurement environment. LCP (~2866ms) tracks FCP plus the poster decode. The preload-ordering lever is now fully exhausted: it eliminated the download bottleneck the plan targeted, but the dominant cost is render/main-thread time pushing FCP to ~2715ms, which preload ordering cannot touch.

verdict.gate_decision: HALT-AT-TASK-1. Per the plan's load-bearing GATING CONDITION, the Lighthouse LCP gate must NOT be flipped warn->error because the measured median LCP (2866ms) did not land under 2500ms. Task 2 (the gate flip) was NOT executed. The hoist + defer landed cleanly (all tests green, structural preload-order proof passes) but did not close the budget miss on this environment.
verdict.environment_note: FCP measured ~2715ms here vs the 07-03 record of ~1817ms — a ~900ms environment delta (different host/Chrome/headless flags than the 07-03 run). The poster-network timing (18ms) confirms the code change is sound; the residual is FCP/render-bound and partly measurement-environment-dependent. A like-for-like re-measure on the 07-03 host, OR on the faster production apex (BASE_PATH=''), may read lower — but on THIS conservative local-root measurement the budget is missed.
next_levers: (a) Re-measure on the faster production apex (BASE_PATH='' — no subpath) and/or on the 07-03 reference host to get a like-for-like FCP baseline before deciding the flip — the ~900ms FCP delta vs 07-03 suggests the 2866ms here is environment-inflated.

(b) Attack FCP directly (the real bottleneck, not the poster download): reduce render-blocking/main-thread work in the critical path — e.g. inline critical CSS, trim the initial JS the first paint waits on, or audit why first paint sits at ~2.7s.
(c) A genuine AVIF poster <picture> variant in HeroAmbient (PERF-V2-02) would shave decode but NOT the dominant FCP cost — lower priority given the network diagnostic.
(d) The _four branch: accept warning-only and defer the blocking flip to post-launch real-user telemetry.
